clinician.final_diagnosis: Carcinomatous Lymphangitis of the Lung (CLC) and Superior Vena Cava (SVC) syndrome
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old woman with a smoking history presented with a persistent cough, leading to a diagnosis of stage IV lung adenocarcinoma. She received triplet therapy (carboplatin, pemetrexed, bevacizumab), which was discontinued due to drug-induced interstitial pneumonia. Two weeks after the onset of interstitial pneumonia, she developed prominent oedema and erythema in her neck and face, followed by dyspnoea. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed severe SVC stenosis, suggesting SVC syndrome. She underwent angiography and balloon dilation for SVC stenosis, but symptoms only temporarily improved, and a follow-up CT showed persistent SVC constriction. A skin biopsy at the erythematic site revealed neoplastic cells within dermal lymphatic vessels, positive for cytokeratin, thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1), and napsin A, confirming carcinomatous lymphangitis of lung origin. The patient died of respiratory failure 1 week after the CLC diagnosis.
